issues.where: There is nothing on earth nor in heaven by which the plants live.
issues.problem: Reverses the sense. tat ... yena = "that by which the plants live is neither on earth nor in heaven"; the draft says no such thing exists.
issues.fix: That by which the plants live is neither on earth nor in heaven.

Note calls the draft a "loose rendering"; after the fix it is literal.
issues.fix: Remove the phrase "the translation nothing ... by which is a loose rendering".

issues.problem: Keep consistent with the vīrudh rendering of unit 1.
yad ... tad is a relative/correlative pair ("what ... that"), not "since/when". The English/Hindi also make rodasī and bhūmiḥ objects although the draft labels them nominative.
issues.fix: Reading: "What the two trembling world-halves and the earth fashioned out, that is moist today and always, like the streams of the ocean." (subject = nominatives; yad = object "what")

issues.problem: yat is the relative pronoun (n. acc. sg.), not a conjunction.
issues.fix: gloss: which, what (relative); gram: n. acc. sg. (relative, correlative of tad)
